entries.question: When will a quantum computer first solve a problem of real commercial or scientific value faster or more cheaply than the best classical method — and which hardware approach gets there first?
Can a classical decoder keep pace with a megahertz-scale surface-code cycle at the code distances a useful fault-tolerant machine needs, or does the control loop become the limiting factor?

Of the proposed routes from quantum computing to more capable AI — quantum-generated training data, sampling advantage, optimisation, and linear-algebra speedups like HHL — which, if any, delivers a real advantage on a problem people care about within ten years?
